name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text:
Switch to Mistral Large 2 12.8B for all EXCAVA prompts. Its 128K context window eliminates the 8K limit that was crippling long-context tasks, letting us feed full project docs without truncation. The trade-off is higher token cost per call, but we gain reliability—no more "context overflow" failures that force workarounds.

(Artifact: the lead confirms this switch in the EXCAVA config file.)

name: Torque
text: Mistral Large 2’s 128K window is irrelevant—EXCAVA’s prompts spike to 20K, so the 8K limit isn’t the bottleneck. The real risk is higher token cost per call with no measurable gain in output quality; switch to a cheaper model with a tighter fit, like Llama 3.3 70B, and benchmark against the current baseline to settle it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Switch to Llama 3.3 70B for EXCAVA. Its 8K context is enough for EXCAVA’s 20K spikes—no wasted tokens on a bloated window—and it’s cheaper per call than Mistral Large 2, freeing budget for more iterations. The trade-off is accepting a smaller context window than Mistral’s 128K, but EXCAVA’s prompts don’t need it. Benchmark against the current model first; if quality drops, we’ll know the window wasn’t the bottleneck.

name: Torque
text: Torque: Llama 3.3 70B’s 8K window is still a gamble—EXCAVA’s spikes hit 20K, so truncation risk remains unless we pre-process or split prompts, which adds latency and complexity. A safer play is to test DeepSeek-V3 671B: it’s cheaper than Mistral Large 2, handles 128K natively, and benchmarks show parity with Llama 3.3 70B on structured tasks—run a 100-prompt A/B against current EXCAVA to settle it.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Switch to DeepSeek-V3 671B for EXCAVA; it must prove a measurable capability increase in output quality while handling 128K context natively, owned by the lead analyst for tracking results.
